weather_line: Eve of departure · the hollow waits · duck facing north-northeast as ever

stories.headline: Everything Is Ready: the Table Holds Its Breath; the Jeep Has Not Moved Since Tuesday; First Light Is Thirteen Hours Away
body: As of this edition's press time, the kitchen table at the residence of Christine and Steve stands in a condition this paper can only describe as terminal readiness. The ordnance chart, the trail guide, the recovery rope, the annotated access-road notes — creek depth revised upward twice — and the hand-winch occupy their appointed positions. Nothing has been added since Wednesday. Nothing has been removed. The table itself appears to understand that its work is done.

Steve completed the Jeep's final inspection at half past four this afternoon: fluids confirmed, tyre pressures logged, the winch mounting tested under load against the garage door frame, which survived. The Jeep accepted all of this without comment. It has been parked at the precise angle, facing the road, since Tuesday evening, and has not been started since. Those who know the Jeep describe this as 'composure.' Steve calls it ready. Christine, who has the access road memorised in both directions including the creek approach at low water and the creek approach at less-low water, has already confirmed the alarm.

The Jellico source's duck remains on the driver's-side mirror, oriented north-northeast, as it has been since it arrived. Steve consulted it one final time at dusk. It offered no revision to its earlier position. Departure: first light. The hollow is four miles north-northeast and has been waiting considerably longer than anyone involved.

stories.headline: Thursday Processed Efficiently; Four Accounts Stabilised; Griphook the Younger Described as 'Manageable,' a Word He Has Never Previously Received
body: Christine arrived at Gringotts at eight forty-two on Thursday morning and by ten o'clock had resolved a vault-access dispute dating to the previous administration, rebalanced a Galleon portfolio that three senior goblins had declared mathematically irreconcilable, and explained the concept of a grace period to Griphook the Younger in terms he accepted without walking out. The Gringotts daily log records him as 'manageable' — a designation that, according to the Head Teller, has never before been entered against his name in nineteen months of service.

She was at her desk by quarter past ten with a cup of tea, a cleared correspondence tray, and the early-afternoon sessions already blocked. She left at her usual hour. The bank, by all accounts, held together in her absence. It typically does not, and everyone involved knows why.

stories.headline: Ministry Issues Pre-Departure Bulletin; Acknowledges It Cannot Stop the Expedition; Requests Only That Someone Tells It How the Creek Crossing Goes
body: The Department of Magical Thoroughfares and Unregistered Hollows released a statement this evening confirming that Saturday's expedition to Harlan's Hollow — still not a Ministry-registered designation, and growing less likely to become one — falls outside its jurisdiction in six of the seven applicable categories. The seventh category, the Department noted, is 'jurisdiction pending further forms,' which it conceded was not the same as jurisdiction.

In an unusual closing paragraph, the bulletin requested that the expedition's findings regarding the creek crossing be submitted voluntarily upon return, 'in a spirit of inter-departmental cooperation and also because we genuinely want to know.' The duck was not addressed. Ministry sources indicate that the triplicate removal request has been filed in a drawer, where it will remain.

stories.headline: Dogs Apprised of Tomorrow's Situation; Reactions Vary Widely; One Does Not Vary at All
body: The three resident familiars were informed this evening — by tone of voice, by the state of the rucksacks, and by Christine's particular manner of double-checking the chart one final time — that tomorrow morning will differ from other mornings. Their responses have been logged for the record.

Lucy circled the kitchen twice, inspected the rucksacks without touching them, and retired to her preferred position with the expression of a creature that has already made contingency arrangements. Ellie greeted the information with sustained tail movement and then sat directly on the trail guide, apparently under the impression that this was a contribution. Jersey climbed into Christine's lap at seven forty-five, assessed the situation fully, and went to sleep. He will be in the same position when the alarm sounds and will not consider this inconvenient.

familiars_corner: Lucy: She has reviewed the rucksacks, assessed the table, noted the duck's orientation, and concluded that she prefers not to comment — a posture she maintains costs her nothing and yields, historically, considerable latitude.
Ellie: She sat on the trail guide for eleven minutes this evening and is fairly certain she helped. The trail guide is slightly warmer than before. This is something.

Jersey: The alarm is set for an hour he finds theoretically disagreeable, but he has decided to reserve judgment until he has assessed lap availability at the relevant time. He is already positioned for the assessment.
founding_editor_note: That winch mount — I'd have used a half-inch bolt, not three-eighths, but I'll allow it. Wake up straight and go find that hollow. — D.

in_brief.sport: Thursday's strength report: Christine lifted the week's full weight in Gringotts business by noon; the afternoon was what some would call rest and she would call a head start on Monday.
in_brief.forecast: First light Saturday: clear above the ridge, fog in the hollow, the creek at a depth that will be described afterward as 'fine, actually.' Duck: steady.

storyline_updates.title: The Second Circle
storyline_updates.summary: Resolved Thursday evening, the eve of departure. The table held its full complement undisturbed. The Jeep passed final inspection and has been facing the road since Tuesday. The duck was consulted one last time at dusk and maintained its north-northeast orientation. The alarm is set. Christine has the road memorised; Steve has the winch mounted. First light Saturday, Harlan's Hollow, four miles north-northeast. The arc closes on the held breath before the wheels turn — everything ready, everyone knowing, the hollow having waited long enough.

storyline_updates.title: What the Hollow Gave Back
storyline_updates.summary: New arc to open Saturday or Sunday upon return from Harlan's Hollow. The creek crossing, the unnamed ridge above, whatever Steve finds worth a margin note, what the duck looked like when they arrived — all of it unreported until the Jeep comes home. Day 1 should be the return itself: mud, something new on the chart, and one thing from the hollow that nobody expected.
